ARCHITECT RETRY NOTE: descendants() repeat-style de-dup must include semantically equal complex JSON objects with different key order, e.g. {"a":{"x":1,"y":2},"b":{"y":2,"x":1}}.

issues.evidence: Spec says descendants() returns all descendants and is shorthand for repeat(children()). Fresh FP-12 EXPLORER probe: descendants().count() = repeat(children()).count() returned false in both native/C++ and forced Python fallback on repeated-looking nested JSON with duplicate primitive and complex values. Probe log: .temp/qa/fp12_explorer_probe.log.
issues.root_cause: Both implementations accumulated every recursive child in descendants() instead of using repeat(children()) de-duplication semantics for newly produced items.
issues.resolution: Updated Python fallback and native C++ descendants() to traverse only newly seen child values using repeat-style semantic keys; added native/fallback regression coverage for repeated-looking nested values and updated null descendant expectations.

issues.spec_citation: FHIRPath Normative Release v2.0.0 §5.8.2 descendants() and §5.2.3 repeat()
issues.evidence: Retry QA probe .temp/qa/fp12_explorer_probe_retry.log: on {"a":{"x":1,"y":2},"b":{"y":2,"x":1}}, native descendants().count() returned 4 while forced fallback returned 3; native descendants().count() = repeat(children()).count() returned false while fallback returned true. The two object children compare equal under repeat(children()) but the native descendants() key path treated serialized key order as distinct.
issues.root_cause: The first remediation used canonical-ish repeat keys, but native JSON object keys were not normalized before hashing, so the descendants() de-dup layer could drift from repeat(children()) equality.
issues.resolution: Native repeat keys now canonicalize JSON recursively with sorted object keys and normalized primitive values before de-duplication; added ordered-key object parity coverage and native sqllogictest coverage.

issues.evidence: Architect audit probe built a 105-level nested resource and evaluated descendants().where($this = 'v104').count(). Native/C++ returned 0 while forced Python fallback returned 1, showing native descendants() silently truncates traversal at depth 100.
issues.root_cause: Native fn_descendants() has a hard depth < 100 loop guard inherited from a safety limit, which drops valid deep descendants instead of traversing until exhaustion.
issues.resolution: Removed the native descendants() depth cutoff and retained the existing result-size safety limit; added a 105-level native/fallback parity regression to the FP-12 tree utility test and QA probe.
